docs.title: How to use test cards
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards
docs.snippet: When you work with a test card, use test API keys in all API calls. This is true whether you’re serving a payment form to test interactively or writing test code.

docs.title: Testing interactively
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards > Testing interactively
docs.snippet: When testing interactively, use a card number, such as 4242 4242 4242 4242. Enter the card number in the Dashboard or in any payment form.

docs.title: Test code
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards > Test code
docs.snippet: When writing test code, use a PaymentMethod such as pm_card_visa instead of a card number. We don’t recommend using card numbers directly in API calls or server-side code, even in testing environments. If you use them, your code might not be PCI-compliant when you go live. By…

docs.title: Review bank debit webhook sequence
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review bank debit webhook sequence
docs.snippet: All bank debit methods follow the processing to succeeded or payment_failed pattern. In test mode, transitions happen after about 3 minutes for account numbers that simulate a delay. These use a 9 prefix or suffix. See the test values for each method in the referenced section.

docs.title: Review voucher-based webhook sequence
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review voucher-based webhook sequence
docs.snippet: Voucher methods issue a payment code that your customer pays out of band. The PaymentIntent enters requires_action immediately after confirmation. The delayed outcome arrives when your customer pays or when the voucher expires.

docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review redirect and delayed notification method

docs.title: Supported bank account types
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Add or update your bank account > Supported bank account types
docs.snippet: You can use various types of bank accounts for your Stripe payouts, including traditional accounts offered by established financial institutions (such as checking and savings accounts), virtual bank accounts (such as N26, Revolut, and Wise), and debit cards for instant payouts…

docs.title: Financial accounts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Add or update your bank account > Financial accounts
docs.snippet: For eligible businesses in the US, payment proceeds settle in your financial account. You only need to add your bank account information for external payouts.

docs.title: Supported accounts and settlement currencies
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Add or update your bank account > Supported accounts and settlement currencies
docs.snippet: Bank accounts generally must be located in a country where the *settlement currency* (The settlement currency is the currency your bank account uses) is an official currency. For example, SEK bank accounts must be based in Sweden. Stripe also allows you to settle and pay out to…

docs.title: Multiple bank accounts for different settlement currencies
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Add or update your bank account > Multiple bank accounts for different settlement currencies
docs.snippet: In supported countries, you can enable settlements and payouts in additional currencies by adding one bank account per supported settlement currency. If you use multiple bank accounts, you must select a default settlement currency, which you can change at any time.

docs.title: Receive Capital payouts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Receive Capital payouts
docs.snippet: If your Stripe Capital application is approved, you can choose to receive your financing proceeds directly into your financial account instead of your external bank account. This gives you access to funds within minutes and enables you to spend those financing proceeds to…

docs.title: Payout schedule
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout schedule
docs.snippet: Your payout schedule determines when Stripe sends money to your bank account. You can select your preferred payout schedule during onboarding or update it any time in the Stripe Dashboard.

docs.title: How payout timing works
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout schedule > How payout timing works
docs.snippet: Choosing a payout schedule doesn’t change how long it takes for your pending balance to become available. It only controls when payouts are sent.

docs.title: Country-specific payout restrictions
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout schedule > Country-specific payout restrictions
docs.snippet: - Brazil and India: Payouts are always automatic and daily. - Japan: Daily payouts aren’t available. The default schedule is manual. You can also choose weekly and monthly payout schedules. - Thailand: The default schedule is daily automatic payouts.

docs.title: Manual payouts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout schedule > Manual payouts
docs.snippet: If you turn off automatic payouts, you must manually send funds to your bank account through the Dashboard or by using the API to create payouts.

docs.title: Settlement timing
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing
docs.snippet: The payout schedule refers to the cadence at which your funds are paid out, for example, day of the week. The settlement timing refers to the amount of time it takes for your funds to become available. Settlement timing varies per country and is typically expressed as “T+X”…

docs.title: Definition of days
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing > Definition of days
docs.snippet: - **Calendar days**: Includes every day, including weekends and holidays. - **Business days**: Only includes working days, typically Monday through Friday, and excludes public holidays.

docs.title: Delay behavior per account country
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing > Delay behavior per account country
docs.snippet: As the platform, you can set delay_days on your connected accounts. The delay applies as a **business day** or **calendar day** delay, based on the country of the connected account. The following table shows which countries apply the delay by business or calendar day.

docs.title: Settlement timing by country
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing > Settlement timing by country
docs.snippet: Use the following collapsed table to determine your country’s settlement timing. The initial settlement timing applies to your first payout, and the default settlement timing applies to subsequent payouts.

docs.title: Country and settlement timing
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing > Country and settlement timing

docs.title: Settlement timing by payment method
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Settlement timing > Settlement timing by payment method
docs.snippet: Bank debit payment methods typically have longer settlement times than card payments because of the underlying banking systems. These payments have a higher risk of returns or reversals, which factors into their longer settlement periods.

docs.title: Accelerate settlement timing
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Accelerate settlement timing
docs.snippet: Stripe offers products and payment methods that have reduced settlement time depending on your location and are subject to eligibility criteria.

docs.title: 2-day ACH settlement
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Accelerate settlement timing > 2-day ACH settlement
docs.snippet: For eligible US merchants, Stripe offers faster ACH settlement that reduces the settlement time from 4 business days to 2 business days from payment creation. For more details about eligibility and activation, see the ACH support page.

docs.title: Instant Payouts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Accelerate settlement timing > Instant Payouts
docs.snippet: With Instant Payouts, you can instantly send funds to a supported debit card or bank account. You can request Instant Payouts any time, including weekends and holidays, and funds usually appear in the associated bank account within 30 minutes. New Stripe users aren’t immediately…

docs.title: Minimum payout amounts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Minimum payout amounts
docs.snippet: The minimum payout amount depends on the lowest amount we can support with our banking partners. For example, if you’re located in the US and you have less than 1 cent (0.01 of 1 dollar) USD in your Stripe account, you must wait until you accept more payments and increase your…

docs.title: Minimum payout amounts per country
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Minimum payout amounts > Minimum payout amounts per country

docs.title: Negative payouts
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Negative payouts
docs.snippet: Each payout reflects your available account balance at the time it was created. In some cases, you might have a negative account balance. For example, if you receive 100 USD in payments but refund 200 USD of prior payments, your account balance would be -100 USD. If you don’t…

docs.title: Payout failures
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout failures
docs.snippet: If your bank account can’t receive a payout for any reason, your bank returns the funds to us. You’ll receive an error with the reason for the failure. It can take up to 5 additional business days for your bank to return the payout and inform us that it failed. If this happens,…

docs.title: Payout fees
docs.heading_path: Receive payouts > Payout fees
docs.snippet: Stripe doesn’t charge you a fee to initiate normal payouts. When you use multi-currency settlement in a non-primary currency, Stripe charges the applicable fee when the funds settle, rather than when you pay them out.
